newsitem.title: FRANCE: FORECAST-French 1997 growth seen at 2.2 pct - CDC.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-French 1997 growth seen at 2.2 pct - CDC.

text.p: State-owned bank Caisse des Depots et Consignations (CDC) said on Monday it expected the French economy to grow by 2.2 percent in 1997 and 2.3 percent in 1998.
The prediction is below the government's GDP growth forecast of 2.3 percent for 1997 and 2.8 percent for 1998 and below predictions made by other forecasters.
"We are less optimistic than others on a growth recovery in Europe in 1998, notably in France and in Germany," said Patrick Artus, the head of Economic Research for CDC.
Artus said weak wages limit demand, which weighs on investment and growth in France.
"The impact of demand on investment is mostly linked to weak wages," he said.
CDC expects disposable income to grow by 1.2 percent in real terms in 1997 and by 1.7 percent in 1998 after rising 0.2 percent in 1996.
CDC sees household consumption growth slowing down to 1.0 percent in 1997 from 2.3 percent in 96 before reaching 2.1 percent in 1998.
Foreign demand will be the main element behind economic growth in France with exports seen rising by 7.3 percent in 1997 and six percent in 1998 after growing 3.6 percent in 1996, CDC said.
